transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Priya Varma (Redwood SE), Markus Li (Bluewave ML Platform Lead), Sana Rafiq (Bluewave Head of Data Science), Jordan Meyers (Bluewave Infra), Eve Turner (Bluewave Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
- Quick demo of model catalog scouting flow; emphasize quantization bench and routing to cheaper variants for tail latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Went through an example picklist: Llama-like 13B quant-8, Mistral-7B fine-tuned variant, and a trimmed proof-of-concept pipeline.
- Discussed kernel mapping and how runtime selects optimized kernels per sequence length; next steps: share bench spreadsheet and schedule POC kickoff.

Topics covered:
- Model scouting workflow and picklists
- Quantization bench (q4/q8) and observed latency/cost tradeoffs
- Routing policies: latency-first vs cost-first and automatic fallback
- Dedicated vs hosted fit for Bluewave's throughput pattern
- Data residency / security quick Q&A

Transcript body:
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Lena): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We figured start with a short run-through of the scouting flow then dive into the quant bench results that Carlos brought. quick intro from Bluewave folks?
[00:18] Speaker 2 (Markus): Yeah, Markus here, I run infra for Bluewave, basically want something we can run in our VPC eventually, but first just want to understand how fast we can get costs down without breaking p95.
[00:29] Speaker 3 (Sana): And I'm Sana. main use is a mixture of summarization and reranking on customer transcripts — so fidelity matters. we care about hallucination risk and latency around 200ms p95 ideally.
[00:42] Speaker 1 (Lena): Great. quick agenda: 1) catalog scout demo, 2) quant bench walk, 3) routing & fallback, 4) Q&A + next steps. Carlos, take it away on the bench.
[00:53] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Cool. so i uploaded a small suite of prompts — about 200 varied elicit prompts — we ran them across 3 candidate variants: Llama-13b q8, Mistral-7b q4, and a trimmed flip of Llama-13b with some kernel-level optimizations. We measured p50/p95 and token cost.
[01:15] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Quick note on terminology: "q8" here means 8-bit quantization; some of our internal paths we call it "q8-fast" which picks slightly different kernels for matmul. sometimes speech-to-text transcribers show q a-te todo, so apologies for typos.
[01:30] Speaker 2 (Markus): Did you run with KV cache warming? our workload is a lot of short-turn dialog so cache matters.
[01:37] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Good call. yes we did two modes: cold-start and warmed-KV cache. For short prompts, warmed paths reduce p95 by ~20-30% on the 13B q8.
[01:50] Speaker 3 (Sana): What's the hallucination delta between q4 and q8? we cannot accept a big drop.
[01:56] Speaker 4 (Carlos): In our suite the Mistral-7b q4 had slightly higher F1 drop on the QA set — maybe 3-5% — but for summarization it was within noise. We annotate with our eval harness so you can choose threshold-based gating.
[02:12] Speaker 1 (Lena): I'll show the catalog UI — the picklist is where you pin candidate models and add bench tags.
[02:19] Speaker 1 (Lena): (screen share) so here we have Scout -> picklist -> bench request. you can add constraints: target throughput, max p95, preferred region, and security profile (e.g., VPC-only).
[02:33] Speaker 5 (Jordan): Can we restrict to models that are KMS-compatible? we use an HSM for key wraps.
[02:38] Speaker 6 (Priya): Yes — the policy tag "kms-hsm" filters variants we only allow for Private deployments. For Hosted we still encrypt at rest but private deployments can integrate with customer KMS.
[02:49] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Back to bench numbers — for the 13B q8 we saw median token latency 24ms, p95 180ms (warmed KV). cost per 1k tokens about $0.42 on the reference hardware. The Mistral-7b q4 had median 14ms p50 and p95 130ms but lower quality for certain QA prompts.
[03:12] Speaker 3 (Sana): Those p95 numbers look good. how deterministic are they in production — like over evening spikes?
[03:19] Speaker 4 (Carlos): They vary with GPU utilization and batching. Redwood's autoscaler tries to keep batch sizes small for low-latency SLOs; we also offer a reserved dedicated pool for steady throughput. If you want predictability, Dedicated is the recommended route.
[03:33] Speaker 2 (Markus): What's the overhead for our VPC private control plane? we can't have control plane traffic egressing without approval.
[03:41] Speaker 6 (Priya): For Private we can run a customer-managed control plane in your VPC; the runtime nodes still communicate over internal network. minimal egress by default. We'll share the architecture whitepaper.
[03:55] Speaker 1 (Lena): switching to routing: here's the policy editor. You can choose latency-first, cost-first, or a hybrid score that weights quality.
[04:05] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Example: you can route 90% to Mistral-7b q4 and 10% to Llama-13b q8 for production; fallback if latency > 300ms or if quality metrics fall below threshold. That way you get cost savings with graceful degradation.
[04:22] Speaker 5 (Jordan): How does the runtime decide kernel selection? we run chips with mixed architectures (A100 + H100-ish).
[04:29] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Runtime probes the model shape and sequence length distribution, then picks optimized kernels. We also keep a kernel compatibility matrix per hardware family. There is a small startup probe cost but it's amortized across many batches.
[04:43] Speaker 3 (Sana): Can we pin a model variant to a region to comply with residency?
[04:47] Speaker 1 (Lena): Yes you can pin a rollout by region or by tenancy. The catalog UI shows region compatibility badges.
[04:54] Speaker 7 (Eve): A silly question — will the picklist let non-engineers choose models? our product people want to highlight recommendations but not break things.
[05:01] Speaker 6 (Priya): We have a curated "recommended" view with safe defaults; you can export recommended sets to non-technical teams as a short list with suggested prompts.
[05:10] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Quick detour — kernel/quant mismatches: some older kernels don't support q4 with certain attention ops; in those cases we fall back to a slower matmul kernel. you'll see that as a p95 bump in the bench. we annotate the bench result with the kernel reason.
[05:28] Speaker 2 (Markus): Would be great to see the raw csv.
[05:31] Speaker 4 (Carlos): I'll share. it includes per-prompt latencies, token counts, cost, and a kernel-compat tag.
[05:39] Speaker 1 (Lena): Let's walk through a concrete sample: Sana's summarization prompt set.
[05:44] Speaker 3 (Sana): Yep, we uploaded a 50-prompt set earlier where each prompt is a customer call transcript snippet.
[05:49] Speaker 4 (Carlos): On that set, Llama-13b q8 hit p95 210ms cold, 160ms warm; Mistral-7b q4 hit 140ms warm but had lower rouge in 6/50 examples.
[06:05] Speaker 3 (Sana): For edge cases where we need higher quality, what's the gating flow?
[06:09] Speaker 4 (Carlos): You can set a quality threshold; if the model's eval score on a rolling set dips below threshold we route that request to the higher fidelity variant or flag it for human review.
[06:21] Speaker 5 (Jordan): On the infra side, any per-request SDS/tags we need to add so routing preserves tenant id?
[06:27] Speaker 6 (Priya): Yes pass-through metadata like tenant_id is preserved and used by routing rules. We also support token-level cost attribution for billing.
[06:36] Speaker 1 (Lena): Quick Q on pricing: Dedicated has committed monthly pricing; hosted is pay-as-you-go. I'll pull up a rough TCO example comparing 3k qps at 128 tokens per request.
[06:49] Speaker 1 (Lena): (shares TCO slide) Example: With a hybrid routing policy you can reduce unit cost by ~30% while keeping p95 under your 200ms goal, depending on sample distribution.
[07:03] Speaker 2 (Markus): That's promising. are there any known regressions when you quantize from float16 to q8? we saw some edge-case tokenization differences in a different vendor.
[07:12] Speaker 4 (Carlos): We do a regression baseline per model. sometimes tokenization mismatches appear if the tokenizer uses tied-BPEs or has rounding differences; we surface those as part of the bench and show which prompts were affected.
[07:27] Speaker 3 (Sana): I want to make sure we maintain compliance. SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves.
[07:33] Speaker 6 (Priya): Redwood supports SOC 2 type II for Hosted and Dedicated options; for Private we can provide more detailed audit exports. we'll attach the certs.
[07:43] Speaker 7 (Eve): Any limits on model size for Private on-prem? like can we bring a 70B model?
[07:49] Speaker 4 (Carlos): On-prem is constrained by your hardware but our runtime supports large models; network and storage for sharded KV matters. For 70B we'd recommend multi-node shards and check kernel support for quantized paths.
[08:03] Speaker 1 (Lena): Want to demo a routing policy in the UI — set it to cost-first with a quality floor.
[08:09] Speaker 1 (Lena): (clicks) add rule: if prompt tag contains "summary-long" route to Llama-13b q8; else route to Mistral-7b q4 up to 85% traffic. add fallback: if p95 > 300ms route to reserved-13b.
[08:29] Speaker 2 (Markus): How do you measure p95 for deciding fallback — is it per-minute sliding window?
[08:34] Speaker 4 (Carlos): It's configurable; default is a 5-minute sliding window measured at the model-route level. You can set shorter windows for aggressive fallbacks.
[08:46] Speaker 3 (Sana): For our RLHF style prompts, are there differences in behavior post-quant? we use reward models downstream.
[08:54] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Reward models are usually smaller and less sensitive, but we recommend running the same reward model quant bench to validate alignment. we'll add that to the bench template.
[09:05] Speaker 1 (Lena): (recap) So next: Carlos will export bench CSV + kernel notes, Lena will send pricing for Dedicated, Bluewave to share the 3 prompt sets. schedule POC kickoff once we see bench and pricing.
[09:18] Speaker 7 (Eve): Could you include a short one-pager for product folks that explains the picklist concept?
[09:23] Speaker 1 (Lena): Sure — we have a "catalog cheat sheet" we can share.
[09:27] Speaker 5 (Jordan): Any gotchas we should be aware of during POC?
[09:30] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Watch for quant-kernel compatibility and coastline of your model sequence lengths. If most of your calls are long context > 2k tokens some quant paths have less benefit. We'll simulate with your samples.
[09:44] Speaker 2 (Markus): We're also evaluating latency budget vs cost savings. Would like to set up a short benchmark that runs overnight to get stable p95 numbers.
[09:53] Speaker 4 (Carlos): We can run a longer batch-run on dedicated infra; we'll need a short window of time and your sample prompts.
[10:01] Speaker 3 (Sana): Small note — in some summaries we noticed entity dropouts in q4; would like to log examples.
[10:07] Speaker 4 (Carlos): we'll surface per-prompt diffs and highlight examples where rouge drops.
[10:12] Speaker 1 (Lena): Any other questions?
[10:16] Speaker 7 (Eve): nothing here.
[10:18] Speaker 2 (Markus): one more: how do rollouts look with canary traffic?
[10:22] Speaker 4 (Carlos): Canary flows are native; you can start with 1% and ramp to 100% with automatic rollback on quality or latency regression.
[10:33] Speaker 1 (Lena): Ok we'll wrap. Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short email with link to bench and pricing.
